title: Microsoft 365 Apps cloud update: up to 10 rollout waves with custom delays for Monthly Enterprise
summary: Hold: the briefing says the deadline reduction is the only change that happens without administrator action, but Microsoft also changes how channel moves follow existing rollout waves. The roadmap details, licensing prerequisites and main controls are supported; the claim that no organisational content is read is not documented.

claims.claim: The roadmap item is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The general availability target is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The preview target is May CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "May CY2026"

claims.claim: The record lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Desktop and Web platforms.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Desktop", "Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the previous wave limit as three.
claims.quote: increased flexibility to configure more than the current limit of three waves

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Administrators can create up to nine custom waves.
claims.quote: Create up to nine custom waves by assigning Microsoft Entra groups, for a maximum of 10 waves.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The maximum total is 10 rollout waves.
claims.quote: Create up to nine custom waves by assigning Microsoft Entra groups, for a maximum of 10 waves.

claims.claim: Rollout waves are built using Microsoft Entra groups.
claims.quote: Rollout waves use Microsoft Entra groups.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Administrators can choose delays between waves of up to seven days per wave.
claims.quote: Set custom delays between rollout waves, up to seven days per wave.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The new Rollout configuration settings page holds both rollout wave and update deadline settings.
claims.quote: The updated experience moves update deadline and rollout wave settings for the Monthly Enterprise profile to the new Rollout configuration settings page.

claims.claim: The experience includes an updated wave chart and waves overview flyout.
claims.quote: Review the expanded rollout schedule in the updated wave chart and wave overview flyout.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Devices scheduled for a channel change now follow their assigned rollout wave.
claims.quote: Channel change now honors rollout waves, so that devices scheduled for channel change follow their assigned wave.

claims.claim: A final wave is included by default and contains remaining Monthly Enterprise devices not assigned to an earlier wave.
claims.quote: A final wave is included by default and contains all remaining devices in the Monthly Enterprise profile that aren't assigned to an earlier wave.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Rollout waves are optional and disabled by default, requiring administrator configuration.
claims.quote: Rollout waves are optional for the Monthly Enterprise profile and disabled by default.

claims.claim: Without waves, Monthly Enterprise devices receive updates over four to five days coordinated with the internal cloud update throttle.
claims.quote: When rollout waves aren't enabled, devices managed by the Monthly Enterprise profile receive updates over four to five days in coordination with the internal cloud update throttle.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; controls[0].note; Open questions
claims.claim: Rollout waves are supported for Monthly Enterprise, not the Current profile.
claims.quote: The Current profile doesn't support rollout waves because Current Channel updates are released more frequently.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[1].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Monthly Enterprise wave delays plus the update deadline cannot exceed 25 days.
claims.quote: For the Monthly Enterprise profile, the combined total for rollout wave delays and the update deadline can't exceed 25 days.

claims.where: What's changing: purpose of the limit
claims.claim: Microsoft says the limit helps devices complete the update cycle within 28 days of release.
claims.quote: This limit helps devices complete the update cycle within 28 days of release.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The update applies a one-time deadline reduction where existing settings exceed 25 days.
claims.quote: If your current settings exceed the 25-day limit, a one-time reduction to the update deadline will be applied with this update to meeting the new requirement.

claims.claim: All other existing rollout wave settings are preserved.
claims.quote: All other existing rollout wave settings are preserved.

claims.claim: Learn gives the enhanced rollout window as June 2026 to July 2026.
claims.quote: Rolling out June 2026 - July 2026.

claims.claim: Learn says enhanced waves are rolling out gradually and may not yet be available in every tenant.
claims.quote: Enhanced rollout waves is rolling out gradually and might not be available in your tenant right away.

claims.where: Why it matters: nothing about staging changes
claims.claim: Nothing about staging changes unless an administrator configures waves, because waves are disabled by default.
claims.quote: Rollout waves are optional for the Monthly Enterprise profile and disabled by default.
claims.fix: Replace this sentence with 'Rollout waves are optional and disabled by default; existing rollout wave settings are preserved apart from the documented deadline reduction.' This avoids suggesting that existing wave users must configure them again.

claims.where: Why it matters: the one thing that happened without anyone acting
claims.claim: The one-time deadline cut is the only change that happens without administrator action.
claims.quote: Channel change now honors rollout waves, so that devices scheduled for channel change follow their assigned wave. All other existing rollout wave settings are preserved.
claims.fix: Replace 'The one thing that happened without anyone acting is' with 'Another change applied by this update is'. Existing wave settings are preserved, while the update also changes channel moves to follow their assigned wave; do not describe the deadline cut as the only automatic change.

claims.claim: The feature reads no organisational content.
claims.quote: Searched: 'cloud update organizational content data privacy rollout waves' and 'Microsoft 365 Apps cloud update rollout waves organizational content data collection'; opened cloud-update, cloud-update-enhancements and cloud-update-waves-deadline. None states this content-access exclusion.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with 'The documented change controls update timing.' Remove the unsupported assertion that no organisational content is read.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Delaying update deployment also delays receipt of the release's security fixes.
claims.quote: Guided setup, recommended policies, and cloud-based orchestration help more devices receive the latest security, quality, and feature updates with each update release.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: group membership
claims.claim: Changing wave group membership can change when a device receives updates.
claims.quote: After you assign devices to the destination profile, Cloud update changes the channel when each device becomes eligible, based on the destination profile's rollout configuration. Rollout waves: consider assigning devices to the first rollout wave.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/cloud-update-profiles-channels to sources. Narrow the risk sentence to 'Wave group membership affects update timing, so review who can maintain those groups.'

claims.claim: Wave group assignment is separate from profile assignment.
claims.quote: Group assignment for rollout waves is separate from profile assignment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The wave schedule starts with each new release, typically Patch Tuesday.
claims.quote: The rollout wave schedule starts with each new update release, typically on Patch Tuesday.

claims.claim: The wave schedule continues during a profile pause or exclusion window.
claims.quote: The rollout schedule continues when a profile is paused or an exclusion window is active.

claims.claim: Waves scheduled during a pause have passed when it ends, and devices needing the update can receive it when the profile resumes.
claims.quote: if you pause a profile on Patch Tuesday and resume it 10 days later, all waves scheduled during that period have already passed. Devices that still need the update can start receiving it when the profile resumes.

claims.claim: Rollout waves do not apply to rollback.
claims.quote: Rollout waves don't apply to rollback.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: early assignment
claims.claim: Devices assigned to Monthly Enterprise later in the month are more likely to update outside the wave schedule.
claims.quote: To help devices follow your rollout wave schedule for their first update, assign them to the Monthly Enterprise profile early in the update release. Devices assigned later in the month are more likely to update outside the rollout wave schedule.

claims.claim: A later-wave device can show completed before its wave starts, including after an online repair.
claims.quote: a device in a later wave can show a completed status before its scheduled wave starts. This status can occur when the device is already up to date when it onboards to cloud update, when an online repair updates the installation

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Cloud update requires Microsoft 365 A3/A5, Business Standard/Premium, Office 365 E3/E5 or Microsoft 365 E3/E5 assigned to the user.
claims.quote: Your user must be assigned to one of the following subscription plans: Microsoft 365 A3; Microsoft 365 A5; Microsoft 365 Business Standard; Microsoft 365 Business Premium; Office 365 E3; Office 365 E5; Microsoft 365 E3; Microsoft 365 E5.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Rollout waves are included under the entitlement required for cloud update.
claims.quote: Licensing requirements: Your user must be assigned to one of the following subscription plans:

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate licence, meter or charge for enhanced rollout waves.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Apps cloud update enhanced rollout waves licensing price meter charge'; opened cloud-update-requirements, cloud-update-enhancements, cloud-update-waves-deadline and cloud-update. Product licences are listed; no separate wave licence, meter or charge was found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: wave groups
claims.claim: User objects in wave groups must have a supported licence assigned.
claims.quote: User objects must be present in Microsoft Entra ID and have a supported license assigned.

claims.claim: Devices must be eligible for and assigned to the Monthly Enterprise profile before inclusion in waves.
claims.quote: Devices must be eligible for and assigned to the Monthly Enterprise profile before you can include them in rollout waves.

claims.where: Scope: Devices; Governance guidance: wave groups
claims.claim: Device objects in wave groups must be Microsoft Entra joined or hybrid joined.
claims.quote: Device objects must be Microsoft Entra joined or hybrid joined.

claims.claim: User and device objects can be placed in the same group.
claims.quote: Both device objects and user objects can be used and also added to the same group.

claims.where: Scope: Groups; Governance guidance: wave groups
claims.claim: A single group should contain no more than 20,000 objects.
claims.quote: Multiple groups can be used, but a single group should contain no more than 20,000 objects.

claims.claim: Nested groups are supported up to three levels deep.
claims.quote: Nested groups support up to three levels deep.

claims.where: Scope: Roles; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Office Apps Administrator is recommended; Security Administrator and Global Administrator can also manage cloud update.
claims.quote: You can use the following built-in Microsoft Entra roles for accessing and managing the feature: Office Apps Administrator (Recommended); Security Administrator; Global Administrator.

claims.claim: Global Reader does not support cloud update.
claims.quote: Global Reader is another built-in role supported by the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center, but it does not support some features like cloud update or the Modern App Settings page.

claims.claim: Cloud update's requirements list GCC, GCC High and DoD, and Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet as unsupported plans.
claims.quote: The following plans are not supported: Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet; Microsoft 365 GCC; Microsoft 365 GCC High and DoD.

claims.claim: Cloud update manages supported Microsoft 365 Apps on supported Windows 10/11 and Windows Server versions that support Microsoft 365 Apps.
claims.quote: Supported version of Microsoft 365 Apps; Supported version of Microsoft Windows 10/11; Supported version of Windows Server that supports Microsoft 365 Apps.

claims.claim: Wave configuration is at Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Cloud Update > Monthly Enterprise > Settings > Rollout configuration > Yes, create rollout waves > + Add waves.
claims.quote: expand Cloud Update, and then select Monthly Enterprise. ... Settings ... Rollout configuration ... Yes, create rollout waves ... Select + Add waves, add your Microsoft Entra groups, set the Delay before next wave value
claims.fix: For a row governing delays as well as wave creation, extend the path to 'Cloud Update > Monthly Enterprise > Settings > Rollout configuration > Yes, create rollout waves > + Add waves > Delay before next wave'. The current path correctly reaches the configuration pane but stops before the delay control.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Graph, PowerShell or REST operation for configuring cloud update waves and delays is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Apps cloud update rollout waves update deadline Microsoft Graph API PowerShell servicing profile configuration' and 'cloud update rollout waves deadline API beta'; opened waves-deadline, enhancements and cloud-update. No wave-setting operation found.

claims.claim: The Monthly Enterprise deadline control is at Cloud Update > Monthly Enterprise > Settings > Rollout configuration > Update deadline in Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
claims.quote: expand Cloud Update, and then select a profile. ... select the Settings tab. ... Select Deadline or Rollout configuration, depending on the profile. ... Adjust the Update deadline slider

claims.claim: No Microsoft Graph, PowerShell or REST operation for setting the cloud update deadline is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Apps cloud update rollout waves update deadline Microsoft Graph API PowerShell servicing profile configuration' and 'cloud update rollout waves deadline API beta'; opened waves-deadline and enhancements. Found the slider, not a deadline-setting API.

claims.claim: The default update deadline is three days.
claims.quote: The default deadline is 3 days.

claims.claim: The update deadline can be configured from zero to 14 days.
claims.quote: You can set the deadline from 0 to 14 days.

claims.claim: The deadline determines when users are prompted to close Microsoft 365 Apps for update installation.
claims.quote: The deadline determines when users are prompted to close Microsoft 365 Apps so updates can be installed.

claims.claim: Wave progress is at Microsoft 365 Apps admin center > Cloud Update > Monthly Enterprise > Overview > View waves overview.
claims.quote: From the Overview tab, select View waves overview to open the flyout. The flyout shows wave details, including the wave name, start date, device count, and rollout status for each wave.
claims.fix: Use 'Cloud Update > Monthly Enterprise > Overview > wave chart > View waves overview'. The also-cited waves-deadline page documents reaching the Monthly Enterprise profile and says 'Under the wave chart, select View waves overview'; the missing heading is not a wrong navigation step.

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell equivalent of the wave schedule and progress overview is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Apps cloud update waves overview progress Microsoft Graph API PowerShell reports'; opened progress-health and cloud-update, and read Graph getM365AppUserCounts search results. That report is app usage, not wave progress; no equivalent found.

claims.claim: The waves overview displays wave start dates, device counts and status for monitoring rather than configuration.
claims.quote: The flyout shows wave details, including the wave name, start date, device count, and rollout status for each wave. Use this information to track wave-level progress

claims.claim: Audit searches are on Audit > Search in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Exchange PowerShell supports Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <ExDateTime> -EndDate <ExDateTime> -Operations <String[]> for filtering audit searches.
claims.quote: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -EndDate <ExDateTime> -StartDate <ExDateTime> ... [-Operations <String[]>]. The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation.

claims.claim: Searching the audit log requires the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs role.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log. ... To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.
claims.fix: Replace the role sentence in controls[3].note and Governance controls with 'Portal searches require Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs in Microsoft Purview; PowerShell searches require those roles in the Exchange admin center and run in Exchange Online PowerShell.'

claims.where: Governance controls; controls[3].governs; Governance guidance: audit log
claims.claim: Cloud update audit records cover wave and deadline configuration changes and identify the administrator responsible.
claims.quote: Audit records help you identify which admin action was performed, who performed it, when it occurred, and which cloud update object was affected. ... Profile configuration changes, such as setting update deadlines or configuring rollout waves.
claims.fix: Qualify the Governance controls audit sentence with 'When auditing is enabled for Microsoft 365,'. The cited cloud-update-purview page states that condition for record generation.

claims.claim: In the Purview activity list, administrators can search for cloud update activities.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, search for cloud update in the activity list, and then select the cloud update activities that you want to include in the search.

claims.claim: The Rollout configuration page has a Total delay counter for reviewing the total before saving.
claims.quote: Use the Total delay counter on the Rollout configuration settings page to review the total delay before you save your changes.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: A three-day deadline leaves 22 days of the 25-day budget for wave delays, and increasing delays can require shortening the deadline.
claims.quote: For the Monthly Enterprise profile, the combined total for rollout wave delays and the update deadline can't exceed 25 days.

claims.claim: At November 2026, Learn documents no API for cloud update profile configuration.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Apps cloud update rollout waves update deadline Microsoft Graph API PowerShell servicing profile configuration' and 'cloud update rollout waves deadline API beta'; read cloud-update, enhancements and profile/channel assignment results. No profile-setting API found.

claims.where: Open questions: deadline reduction calculation and notice
claims.claim: The exact deadline-reduction calculation and any notice to affected administrators remain undocumented in the examined public guidance.
claims.quote: Searched: 'cloud update one-time reduction deadline calculation notice'; opened cloud-update-enhancements and cloud-update-waves-deadline. The reduction is stated, but no formula or affected-tenant notice is described; no Message Center post was supplied.

claims.claim: The action rating is review because this change is wholly optional.
claims.quote: action: review; Where a tenant's existing settings exceed 25 days, Microsoft applies a one-time reduction to the update deadline with this update
claims.fix: Set action to 'prepare': this update arrives for existing customers and includes a deadline adjustment to check, rather than only a control that changes nothing until newly chosen. Risk and cost are low, so an act-now rating is not required by the scale.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist tells administrators to configure or take stock of has a controls-table row.
claims.quote: Assign devices to the Monthly Enterprise profile early in a release month so their first update follows the wave schedule. ... Controls cover waves, deadlines, waves overview and audit search.
claims.fix: Remove the At rollout bullet that tells administrators to assign devices to the Monthly Enterprise profile; profile assignment has no controls-table row. Keep the existing factual explanation of early assignment in Risk assessment.
